turns.content: At 25 C, enough stoichiometric AgCl is dissolved in aqueous ammonia to give 0.010 M total dissolved silver. Because dissolution also gives 0.010 M chloride, use Ksp(AgCl) = 1.56 x 10^-10 to determine the free Ag+ concentration. The desired final quantity is the analytical ammonia concentration initially charged, not just free NH3 at equilibrium.
Let L=[NH3]free. Using beta1 = 2.1 x 10^3 and beta2 = 1.7 x 10^7, write [Ag(NH3)+] and [Ag(NH3)2+] in terms of free Ag+ and L, then impose the 0.010 M total-silver balance.
Solve that silver-balance equation for the physically meaningful free-ammonia concentration L.
Use the resulting L and free Ag+ to calculate the concentrations of Ag(NH3)+ and Ag(NH3)2+.
Now account for both free and coordinated ligand. Evaluate the analytical ammonia inventory L + [Ag(NH3)+] + 2[Ag(NH3)2+].
Verify the silver and ammonia balances numerically and identify which dissolved silver species predominates.
Give the required analytical ammonia concentration and distinguish it clearly from the equilibrium free-ammonia concentration.
